(a) the dynamics of cell division is governed by the interplay of two distinct mechanisms, namely the cell size control and the cell cycle control; and (b) cell division can be described as the interplay of a dynamical system (the cell cycle) and a stochastic system (the cell size regulation), and that the cell size regulation is a stochastic process that is driven by noise
(1) the cell is a complex system with multiple levels of organization and (2) the cell is able to self-organize and self-repair.

(i) a single cell can produce a variety of cell types by regulating the expression of genes in a combinatorial manner, (ii) this process is regulated by the interplay of the cell's internal state (e.g., the concentration of transcription factors) and external signals, and (iii) this interplay can be captured by a simple model of the regulatory network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and analysis of computational methods to model and simulate the dynamics of biological cells.

the mathematical modelling and computer simulations of the dynamics of biological systems, in particular of cellular processes and systems, and the development of new methods and tools for their analysis.
the development of computational and mathematical methods for the analysis of complex biological systems.

the field of computational cell biology is still in its infancy, but it is rapidly developing.
the modelling and simulation of biological cells is a very active and rapidly evolving research area that is of central importance for modern biology and biomedicine.
, despite the fact that we are far away from being able to simulate a cell in its full complexity, we are now able to model and simulate many of its important processes.

we have been able to demonstrate that the use of computational methods and tools is a powerful means to study the behaviour of biological systems and, in this way, to contribute to the understanding of their function and malfunction.

the computational and mathematical modelling of biological cells has become an essential part of the toolbox of modern bioscience.

computational modeling and analysis can be used to understand how cells sense their environment and how this sensing can be used to control cell behavior.
